title: YOUR RIGHT TO A STATE NATIONAL PASSPORT
summary: Narrated promoter treatise on getting a 'state citizen' passport, promising freedom from taxes, tickets, lawsuits, debt and detention.

assertions.quote: when the officer runs your id he or she will see your status and has to let you go
a state citizen is not and no constitutional tax can be levied against a state citizen and congress is not authority over state citizens
it was created by the congressional act of 1871
once you receive your passport you should never have to pay taxes you can carry any gun you should not get tickets

verdicts.note: A passport has no effect on tax, traffic or debt obligations; people relying on this are prosecuted and foreclosed on.

assertions.quote: put without prejudice above your signature this ensures that you are not a legal fiction and are not contracting away your rights
once you have the state citizen passport do not answer a lawsuit they cannot even get default judgment against you

verdicts.note: Failing to answer a properly served suit leads to default judgment for anyone, whatever status they claim.

assertions.quote: a u.s citizen is a legal fiction slash u.s corporation and has no rights secured by the constitution

verdicts.note: US citizens hold full constitutional rights; the 14th Amendment makes them citizens of both the nation and their state.

assertions.quote: if you check off yes to u.s citizen on anything then that makes you a u.s citizen otherwise you are a state citizen

verdicts.note: Citizenship is set by birth or naturalization law, not by boxes ticked on a form; the passport still records US nationality.

Citizenship or nationality is fixed by place and parentage of birth, and a valid US passport is conclusive proof of US citizenship; nothing lets a form answer create a separate 'state citizen' status.

assertions.quote: for a crime to exist there must be an injured party

verdicts.note: Legislatures define many offences without a victim, such as unlicensed driving or possession, and courts enforce them.
